Hi Julie —

Sorry for the friction here. Thanks for the screenshot. I've looped in Ben from Operations (support) and Naomi from onboarding so we can triage quickly. A couple quick asks that will help us debug:

- Can you forward the original invite email as an attachment (not a copied screenshot) so we can see the raw headers?
- If possible, try opening the invite link from the original invite message on a mobile device (not a forwarded message or an email thread). Sometimes forwarding alters headers or adds S/MIME signing that our redirect layer treats as a signed payload.
- Could you also paste the full error text (if there's a stacktrace or request id) — the screenshot is helpful but the exact message helps map to logs.

Workaround for now: If you can paste the invite link into a new private/incognito window and open it directly (again coming from the original invite email) that often bypasses the forwarded-message wrapping. If that doesn't work, we'll escalate to engineering and provide a temporary manual activation.

Ben/Naomi — could you pick this up? If it's a signature param on the invite redirect we should be able to either strip the param or accept signed forwards from these vendor domains as a short-term fix.

I'll follow up with a proposed SLA credit if this blocks the PO timeline.

Thanks Julie — and thanks Sean for the ping. Quick technical note from the ops side:

- I pulled the request id (you included in the screenshot: req=0a3f2c) and matched it in the redirect proxy logs. The redirect returns HTTP 400 with body: "error: invitation_rejected, reason: signature_verification_failed, param: sig".
- That "sig" parameter is appended when an S/MIME or enhanced email client re-signs the original invite link when a message is forwarded. When the link contains an extra query param we validate the signature on the invite token and the mismatch triggers the rejection.

Immediate troubleshooting steps (low friction):
1) Please open the original invite email (not a forwarded copy) and tap/click the link directly from that message. If you received it in a thread where it was forwarded, forwarding can add the param.
2) If you can't access the original, copy the invite token (the long alphanumeric string after "/invite/") from the original email and paste it into this form: https://internal.redwood.com/proxy/accept-invite (I will send a temporary one-time-use acceptance link once you paste it).

Longer-term fix: Naomi and I will add a small normalization step to strip non-whitelisted query params from invite redirects for known partner domains, and add defensive checks in the validator to ignore the extra "sig" when the base token matches. We can ship a patch in the next sprint; I'll include a quick retrofit to avoid blocking live onboarding this week.

Julie — can you forward the original invite message to ben.carter@redwood.com as an attached .eml? That will give us the raw headers and the token. Also if you can attach the W-9, attach vendor_w9.pdf so Naomi can start the record while we troubleshoot.

Attachment: mutual-action-plan.xlsx (xlsx)

—Ben
